paragraphs.text: LAN session sync for DSH: auto-discover devices running this plugin, browse/pull/push sessions over
HTTP with SHA-256 verification, and keep a local-only nickname per device. ｜ DSH 局域网会话同步：自动发现装了本插件的设
备、仅存本机的设备命名、浏览/拉取/推送会话，带 SHA-256 校验。
# dsh-session-sync
**LAN session sync for DSH.** Every DSH that has this plugin discovers the others on the local netwo
rk, lists their sessions, and can pull or push conversations over plain HTTP. The nickname you give
a device lives **only on your machine** — the peer can go offline, reboot, or change IP and come bac
k, and you still see the name you gave it.
🌏 简体中文 · **English**
> **0.8.0 UI rebuild**: session desk, whole-row selection, selection bar, transfer dock and settings
were redrawn. The full draft (19 scenes, dark/light, zh/en) is in `docs/redesign/index.html`; imple
mentation mapping and acceptance are in `DESIGN.md`. The whole-session file transfer design (chunks
/ resume) is in `session-bundle-transfer.md` (next phase).
## ✨ Features

| **📡 Zero-config discovery**
UDP broadcast on every IPv4 interface with a 4s beacon. A peer that ju
st appeared gets an immediate unicast reply, so new devices show up without waiting for the next rou

nd. | **🏷️ Local-only nicknames**
Stored in `<home>/session-sync/state.json` and keyed by a stable *
*device id** (uuid) — not IP, not hostname. The peer renaming itself never overwrites your label. |

| **🗂️ Browse · pull · push**
See each device's sessions with title, cwd and time; pull one into thi
s machine or push one of yours out. Imported rows are marked as pulled. | **🔐 SHA-256 verification**
Exports carry `sha256 = SHA-256(JSON.stringify({format, session, events}))`; imports compare it **b
efore writing a byte** and refuse with HTTP 409 `checksum-mismatch`. Each row has a *Verify* action.

|
| **🔁 Optional auto-pull**
Every 20s, pull sessions you have not pulled yet. Content fingerprints
(not ids) stop two machines with auto-pull on from bouncing one conversation back and forth forever

. | **🎨 Native look, i18n**
Built from DSH design tokens (colors, radii, type scale, 0.2s transition
s), so light/dark follow the host. Language follows DSH by default, with explicit 中文 / English overr

ides. |
| **🔎 Find sessions fast**
Search (press `/`), 全部 / 未拉取 / 已拉取 filters, sort by time or title
, and ↑↓ / Space / Enter navigation. Rows stay quiet: one status chip, with 校验 and 拉取 on hover or fo

cus. | **🧰 Tidy devices & queue**
The rail only selects; rename, copy address, refresh, push and for
get live in the stage header ⋯. Transfers sit in a bottom dock that expands into the queue; network/

advanced options stay folded. |
| **🪟 Master / detail**
Devices sit in a left column (session count
+ chevron, the whole row is the target) while the selected device's sessions stay visible on the rig
ht — no hidden "click a card to expand". The first online device is selected automatically. | **🧭 De

vice actions**
Push here, rename, copy address, refresh and remove live in the stage header ⋯; renam

e happens inline in the header. |
| **🖱️ Drag, select, drop**
[该节后续省略]
### Three UI promises
- **“This device” is always the first row, and one IP is never two devices.** The card shows this ma
chine's name, `LAN address:sync port` and running version. Any peer whose address belongs to this ho
st is grouped underneath it as “other DSH instances on this machine” (browsable and pushable, so cro
ss-profile sync still works) instead of counting as a device — the list and its counters only ever m

ean **other machines**.
- **Untitled sessions carry `#first-8-chars-of-session-id`.** A pile of “Unt
itled” rows looks identical; the id is what tells them apart. The pull plan's “already present” flag
is keyed by the same peer + session id, so renaming a session never turns a duplicate into a fresh

copy.
- **A crashing UI is never blank.** Render errors hit an error boundary that prints platform,
Node version, host version, ports, UA and a stack summary, with *Reload* / *Copy diagnostics*. If Wi
ndows still shows nothing, paste that block into an issue.

## 🧭 Where it lives
A **Session Sync** row appears under **Plugins** in the left sidebar (`sidebar.panellist` + keyed `m
ain` panel, id `session-sync`). The same component is also registered as **Settings → Session Sync**
(`settings.section`).

- **This machine** — the name other devices see; changing it broadcasts immediately.
- **Devices** —

online/offline, last heartbeat, session count, platform and version.
- **Rename / Forget** — a per-
device nickname for this machine only. Offline devices keep their row (and their nickname), greyed o

ut.
- **Sessions / Pull / Push** — list a peer's sessions, copy one here, or send one over.
- **Veri
fy** — re-fetch the peer's payload, recompute SHA-256 and compare it with the local copy (`sha256 2b

12f7854d80… verified`).
- **Integrity, not identity.** A digest proves the bytes match; it does not
prove who sent them — anyone can recompute it. So verification stays automatic and fail-closed, and
there is no per-transfer “confirm the hash” prompt (that only trains people to click through). When
you genuinely need authenticity, copy the full digest and compare it out-of-band (phone, terminal);

the copy action sits next to the verified row.
